shots.title: Resolve SLOPE state from the git common-dir owner so repo worktrees share one store (#665/#667)

hazards.description: [code review] Worktree-only initialization did not resolve descendants when the primary checkout lacked SLOPE state.
[architect review] First-time initialization from an unconfigured git descendant could create nested SLOPE state.

shots.notes: Added one repository-state owner resolver based on git common-dir semantics and routed configuration, SQLite creation, sessions, claims, sprint state, review state, baselines, and repository-scoped ignored files through it. Branch-local tracked roadmap and source reads remain worktree-local.

shots.title: Make hook briefing, guard baselines, session state, and MCP tools agree on the same store path inside worktrees (#665)

hazards.description: [architect review] MCP execute, context, map, and related tools did not retain the discovered source root.

shots.notes: Aligned CLI hooks, MCP project discovery, guard baselines, session identity, interview state, direct semantic-index consumers, store backup/restore, and generated testing worktrees with the common repository state owner.

shots.title: Warn when an in-repo child worktree would be globbed by parent tooling (#667)

hazards.description: [architect review] In-repository worktree warnings compared lexical paths and could be bypassed through symlinks.

shots.notes: Added an explicit warning for visible child worktrees while preserving the managed ignored worktree directory. Canonical existing-ancestor resolution prevents symlink aliases from bypassing the warning.

shots.title: Add cross-worktree claim, briefing, and guard regressions proving shared coordination (#665/#667)

hazards.description: The first implementation pass covered shared configuration and primary store entry points but independent review found direct SQLite consumers, generated-worktree copying, init/interview, nested project discovery, legacy claims, and rejection cleanup still needed the same ownership contract.

The first full-suite run exposed nested fixture projects accidentally resolving to the live checkout state; the fixtures and review-tier test were isolated, and the live sprint-state hash now remains unchanged across the complete suite.
[architect review] Direct semantic-index consumers and store backup/restore bypassed the shared state resolver.
[architect review] Linked-worktree init and interview could overwrite primary state or create partial local state.
[architect review] MCP testing sessions and autonomous loop worktrees copied or symlinked .slope state.
[architect review] Nested SLOPE projects beneath a repository root were not consistently discovered.
[code review] Stop-check trimmed leading porcelain status whitespace and misclassified unstaged baseline files.
[code review] Legacy file-backed claims were hidden whenever the shared store opened successfully.
[code review] Briefing store handles were not closed when execution or claim reads rejected.
[code review] Project custom workflows were loaded from the linked worktree and workflow-step-gate failed open.
[code review] Cross-session memory selected a worktree-local JSON backend instead of the shared SQLite or JSON owner.
[code review] First-time CLI and MCP initialization from a git descendant split tracked project artifacts from repository state.
[code review] Checkout-root source resolution overrode explicitly configured nested SLOPE projects.

shots.notes: Added real linked-worktree tests for shared claims, MCP discovery and source-root propagation, briefing, Git baselines, semantic-index commands, backup/restore, init/interview protection, custom workflow enforcement, shared memory backends, canonical child-path warnings, legacy claim merging, and store cleanup on failure. Final verification passed 258 test files and 4,281 tests, with 26 skips, plus typecheck and build.

conditions.description: The fix crosses CLI, MCP, hooks, guards, session state, SQLite ownership, generated worktrees, and test isolation, so every repository-state consumer had to agree on one boundary.
Two independent review lanes requested changes after the initial implementation and expanded regression coverage was required before approval.

special_plays: Kept tracked roadmap and source reads branch-local while sharing only repository-scoped ignored coordination state.
Verified the full test suite cannot mutate the live S261 state by comparing the state-file hash before and after all 4,281 tests.

training.description: A shared-state migration must inventory direct constructors, maintenance commands, generated worktrees, initialization paths, and compatibility registries, not only the central store factory.
training.outcome: S261 now has command-level actual-git coverage across those entry points.

training.description: Repository ownership and nested project discovery are related but distinct: linked worktrees adopt the primary owner, while an explicit nested SLOPE project keeps its own state.
training.outcome: The resolver and MCP discovery tests cover both descendants of nested projects and legacy copied configs at linked-worktree roots.

nutrition.description: 258 test files passed; 4,281 tests passed and 26 were skipped.
TypeScript typecheck and the root plus pi-extension production build passed on Node 22.
The primary sprint-state SHA-256 remained unchanged across the full test suite.

bunker_locations: Direct SqliteSlopeStore construction bypasses resolveStore and must explicitly resolve repository state ownership.
Generated worktrees must never copy or symlink .slope state; git common-dir ownership is the only supported sharing mechanism.
Porcelain status parsing must preserve the two-character status column, including a leading space for unstaged changes.
yardage_book_updates: Use resolveRepoStateCwd for repository-scoped ignored state and resolveRepoStatePath for configured state files.
Use the current worktree for tracked roadmap and source files; sharing those reads would erase branch-local reality.
Place generated testing worktrees beside the repository or under the ignored managed worktree directory.
course_management_notes: Carry the shared-owner contract into S262 status work so operator output describes the same sessions and claims seen by guards and MCP.
Keep explicit nested SLOPE fixture projects isolated from the enclosing repository owner in tests.
